verdict: NOT READY FOR GATE 0 as written. The V1-derived beat evidence is largely accurate (because the outline is a scene-by-scene transplant of 4l97aNza_Zc, not a synthesis of "laws"), but the credit budget rests on a misread statistic, six of the fourteen "N of 10" laws are overstated by the outline's own evidence lists, the hook targets quote 60-s and th-0.1 numbers as if they were 45-s/hard-cut numbers, the story has two internal rule/arithmetic breaks, and the pushback section asserts an "original premise" that the outline itself contradicts with near-verbatim V1 dialogue. Fix list before Gate 0: (1) replace the "31/88 = 35% yield" with a real roll-1 pass rate from the Grok logs (Dinoverse Z9 9/10 roll-1, christ_cares 7/7 zero retakes, cookies 36/36 held) and model the WEEKLY cap that actually blocked production 2026-07-09; (2) reconcile the per-beat clip lists (sum = 88) with the budget (156) and re-cost against the clip-variety rule, which forbids the x40/x20/x10 reuse the budget assumes; (3) fix the planet ladder (20 M minus 5 m/day from Day 25 reaches 0 M on Day 29, not 2 M) and the red-line/pod contradiction (Beat 5 says entering the pod = quit = $0 for both; Beat 20 says launching the pod = $1M steal); (4) rewrite every lifted V1 line into original dialogue and re-count PIP's on-camera lines (~30 in the outline vs the budget's own <=20 cap); (5) restate the laws with honest counts and re-estimate the script at ~3,900-4,100 words (V1-V3 run 197-213 wpm), not 2,800; (6) strike the implied SuperGrok Heavy path and Remotion, or flag both as new spend/new tools for the owner.
attacks_that_land: CREDIT BUDGET IS BUILT ON A MISREAD NUMBER. The outline's yield anchor 'the repo's own banked yield is 31/88 = 35% (Wild Bird EP02)' is a PROGRESS counter, not a reject rate: memory project_wildbirdsurvival_teardown.md line 147 says 'CLIP BANK: 31 of 88 shots banked (disk-verified ... remaining = S032+)'. Nothing in the repo says 57 clips were generated and rejected. Actual Grok roll-1 evidence in memory: Dinoverse Z9 '9 clean roll-1', christ_cares direction test 'zero retakes' 7/7, cookies 36 clips held identity — i.e. roll-1 pass is closer to 80-90% with a 3-roll cap. The 240-310 generation figure and the '12-16 days' conclusion inherit the error. VERIFY-BEFORE-CLAIM violation on the single number that prices the project.

THROUGHPUT MODEL IS THE WRONG ONE AND THE WEEKLY CAP IS NEVER MENTIONED. The outline uses 'SuperGrok ≈ 20 clips/24 h' (project_creator_masterclass_research.md, a web-research note from 2026-08-03). The later, empirically proven recipe (reference_grok_imagine_batch_recipe_2026-08.md, 2026-08-19) says the paid account ytmanager628 runs '~36 clips/hour, 3 tabs, unlimited-ish'. The limit that has actually stopped production in this repo is the WEEKLY cap (project_dinoverse_production.md: 'You've hit your weekly limit, resets July 13', 2026-07-09; a ~40-clip week used 25%). The budget section contains zero mention of a weekly cap, so the only binding constraint is unmodeled. The 'Heavy ≈ 80+/12 h → 2-4 days on Heavy' line presents a $300/mo tier ($270/mo delta) as a viable fast path without flagging it as new spend — this is the subscriptions-only / no-spend-without-prototype violation in the doc.

CLIP COUNT IS INTERNALLY INCONSISTENT BY ~2x. Summing the outline's own per-beat 'unique clips' gives 88 (hook 16, Act1 26, Act2 15, Act3 14, Act4 12, Act5 5); the credit_budget section says 156 (14/41/34/21/32/14). Either the beat plan is under-specified by 68 clips or the budget is padded — the document does not agree with itself, so Gate 2's 'actual yield re-prices the budget' has no baseline to re-price.

THE REUSE ASSUMPTION VIOLATES THE CHANNEL'S CLIP-VARIETY RULE. The budget only reaches its number by re-using THE COUNT hover loop x40, two confessional-booth clips x20, two reaction CUs x10, and cutting a 90-s fight (4:50-6:20) at ~1.2 s from 5 unique clips. feedback_clip_variety_rule.md: 'every 6-second beat gets a DISTINCT vantage ... no two ADJACENT clips share a vantage or backdrop.' The measured V1 grammar re-uses ONE take via punch-ins within ~10 s, not the same 6-s clip across 20 minutes. Re-costing under the variety rule pushes unique clips toward 170-240 (one per 5-7 s cut), not 88-156.

SIX LAWS ARE OVERSTATED BY THE OUTLINE'S OWN EVIDENCE LISTS. Law 1 '8 of 10 put a $ figure before 0:17': the list shows V1, V3, V5, V6, V9, V10 = 6 (V2 has no $, V4 none, V7 at 1:08, V8 none). Law 2 '6 of 10 commitment inside 40 s': V5's red line is at 1:15 → 5. Law 8 'genre flip at ~64-85%, 8 of 10': only V1 (64%), V7 (74%), V4 (85%, and it is a ladder, not zero-sum) fall in the window; V3 1:29 is 4%, V9 10:20 is 28%, V10 41%, V5 95%, V2 'rapid fire' is a pace change. Law 10 '7 of 10': V9 'It's emotional' and V8 'I'm gonna fricking cry' are not motive/secret/family beats → 5. Law 12 'nobody leaves with $0, 7 of 10': V1 $125K each and V3's $50K card go to WINNERS, V4's fans win throughout — true consolation-to-losers cases are V5, V7, V9, V10 = 4. Law 13 '10 of 10 ≤30 s after the payoff': V3 resolves at 36:11-36:27 and runs to 37:24 ('just for fun' beam + moral + CTA) = ~58 s. Law 6 'physical irreversible loss, 7 of 10' counts V1's chain-cut (a constraint tightening) and V8's tide (not host-performed) — solid cases are V3, V5, V7, V10.

HOOK TARGETS QUOTE THE WRONG MEASUREMENTS. Re-parsed research/mrbeast_teardown/hook_grammar/scene_scores.txt: at th 0.3 the counts are 0-45 s = 23 (28 is the 0-60 s figure the outline turns into '≥28 shot changes/45 s'); Phase C 16.8-33 s = 13 hard cuts (17 is the th-0.1 count, which includes zooms/flashes), so 'mean shot 0.95 s' is really ~1.25 s. 'Every cut within ±0.12 s of an onset': 9 of 13 Phase C cuts are within ±0.12 s; 20.52 (+0.17), 26.66 (+0.16), 29.76 (+0.22) are not, and 28.09 sits +0.98 s from the nearest onset. The silent hold 'loudness −12.1/−12.8 for 4.1 s' is two 0.5-s samples at −12; the ebur128 log shows 14.11 = −9.9, 14.61 = −8.5, 15.11 = −9.7 — the dip is intermittent, not sustained. The outline's hook will be graded at Gate 2 against targets the reference itself does not meet.

STORY LOGIC BREAKS TWICE. (a) Ladder arithmetic: Day 25 sets 20 M and 'loses 5 metres a day until Day 30' → 15/10/5/0 by Day 29; the outline shows 2 M on Day 29 and 'a rock the size of a car' on Day 30 — Law 4's 'count shown at every step' cannot be rendered consistently. (b) Rule contradiction: Beat 5 says crossing the red line INTO THE POD = quit = 'Neither of you wins anything'; Beat 20 says launching THE POD alone = all $1,000,000. Same object, opposite outcomes, no override line. V1 avoids this because the red line and the handcuff keys are separate devices.

THE 'ORIGINAL PREMISE' CLAIM IN THE YPP PUSHBACK IS FALSE ON ITS FACE. Pushback #3 says 'copy the LAWS, not the show — original premise, original characters', but the outline lifts V1's dialogue nearly verbatim at 25+ points: 'I'm locked in', 'Oh gosh', 'He's salty', 'I can't force you two', 'easier with a stranger', 'absolutely insane', 'star/accessory' → 'frontman/accessory', 'Fresh start? / Sure', 'Friends? / Friends.', 'bawling', 'I don't feel well. Mentally.', 'Yeah… no', 'Do you feel regretful now?', heart-shaped breakfast, the self-help book gag, 'You still wear it?', 'The night before we leave is when I'll tell you', five platters with a free option revealed after, 'come at a cost / Oh… it can', 'fundamentally change this entire video', 'This is where the video gets fun', 'perfect revenge story', soundproof box + 'It's a good question', '12h43m', 'fair for me to take', 'A minute and 12 seconds', '16 seconds, you sure? / Nah, half / I might deserve all of it', 'I was NOT expecting that', 'Looks like the band's back. Subscribe.' Format rules are not protectable; a script's dialogue is. This is a derivative adaptation of one video, which is both a copyright exposure the pushback never names and the strongest possible 'template' signal for the YPP reviewer.

PIP'S LINE COUNT BREAKS THE BUDGET'S OWN CAP. The budget names 'PIP is the only mouth in the cast, keep her on-screen dialogue ≤20 lines' as cost driver #1. Counting the outline: PIP has ~30 lines, at least 12 of them in CU or confessional (0:17 money-wall CU, 2:45 CU, the fight, the campfire talk, truth beam x3, five confessionals, 18:35 climax). The 're-use the 2 confessional booth clips x20 with new VO' plan puts a visible small mouth under mismatched dialogue twenty times — the exact failure lens in feedback_i2v_talking_creature_qa.md.

ELEVENLABS ESTIMATE IS ~30% LOW. The three fully mapped references run 197 wpm (V1, 7,289 words/37 min), 213 wpm (V2), 203 wpm (V3). A 20-min video in this grammar is ~3,900-4,100 words ≈ 23-24k characters, ≈ 29-30k with the 25% reserve, not 16.5k/21k. Not a plan-breaker (well under a 100k/mo tier), but it is the number the SHA-locked one-pass script will be measured against, and the 5,000-char box means ~6 chunks per pass, not the implied single generation.

AI-FACES RULE IS MISCHARACTERIZED. feedback_ai_faces_use_real_photos.md is about a REAL PERSON's likeness (Sam Neill), refined 2026-07-15 into 'a QUALITY bar, not an absolute ban' with Grok producing a convincing likeness. It says nothing about AI humans in fiction. The creature cast may still be the right call for the repo's proven strength, but the pushback defends it with a rule that does not exist. Meanwhile the real consistency risk it introduces is uncosted: ORB is a sphere with 'two tiny articulated arms' asked to spread arms, point a finger, hold anklets, snap, and read cards across 40+ clips.

AUTHENTICITY PUSHBACK STOPS AT THE STAGE AND IGNORES THE CLICK LAYER. Pushback #1 says 'do NOT pretend it is real', yet the default cold open promises 'I will give them ONE MILLION DOLLARS' and 4 of 5 title candidates carry '$1,000,000'. The masterclass memory says the CLICK layer decides views; a disclosed-animation title that sells a prop prize is exactly the trust problem the pushback names, and only candidate #5 resolves it. The Squid Game analogy is misapplied: it is scripted drama in a drama genre; Laws 1 and 12 exist in the challenge genre BECAUSE the money is real.

ONE-OFF CLAIM CONTRADICTED. Pushback #3's mitigation is 'one-off episode (no batch of near-identical sequels)', but the cast section sells THE COUNT as 'a mascot the channel can keep across videos' and candidate #2 adopts the 'Last To Leave' series template. The 'per-video edit-fingerprint diff' mitigation is meaningless for a one-off.

WEAK OR WRONG CITATIONS IN SPOT-CHECKED BEATS. Beat 9:45-10:25 cites 'V4 Chandler x3 (11:24, 13:15, 17:10)': the V4 transcript at 13:15 is 'Aww! Your dad just won fifty grand' and 17:10 is '[Karl] Oh!!' — only 11:24 is Chandler. Beat 19:30-19:55 cites V7 28:31 and V9 36:39-36:44 (Law 12) — both are consolation to LOSERS, while the outline's beat pays the winners. Beat 1:30-2:00 flash-forwards 'a countdown clock at 00:03', pre-spoiling that nobody launches early; V1's clock flash-forward is at 35:05, 1.5 minutes before the finale, not at 2:37.

NEW-TOOL AND UNNAMED-TOOL LEAKS. 'hand-built graphics (FFmpeg/Remotion)' introduces Remotion, absent from the repo (hard rule 3: never invent parallel solutions; the engine is scripts/ffmpeg_production_render.py). The '720p→1080p upscale pass on every clip' names no tool. Both need to be either struck or presented to the owner as additions.
attacks_refuted: V1-derived beat timestamps are accurate. Spot-checked against the supplied beat maps and the hook ledger: 0:00-0:12 (punch-out 1.375, photo stack 3.5-5.75, 'EXES' 7.0, '30 DAYS' at 8.25 leading the spoken '30', bloom 11.5) matches the ledger; 0:12-0:17's three cuts at 12.746/13.514/14.348 match the th-0.3 count (3); 0:21-0:30's click onsets are real (25.867 and 29.071/29.164 in onsets.t) and the smirk-hold dip to −13.0/−16.4/−13.4/−15.7 LUFS at 27.6-29.1 s is in the ebur128 samples; 2:45-4:10 (V1 4:29 'cut the chain in half', V3 4:42/7:14), 8:45-9:45 (V1 13:51/13:57/14:03/14:40/15:01), 12:45-13:30 (23:38/37:01 = 63.8%, outline 12:45/20:00 = 63.75%), 13:30-15:10 (V1 24:56-28:16), 18:35-19:30 (V1 35:05-36:34) all check out.

Cross-video citations for the truncated maps are real. Verified in research/mrbeast_teardown/*/transcript.txt: V4 27:12 'Subscribe!'; V5 0:44 'I have no job after this' and 1:15 red line; V7 27:52 'You have seconds left', 28:31 '$20,000 each', 28:38 subscribe; V8 1:31 'Little did we know' and 30:02 next-video tease; V9 10:20 'fundamentally change the video', 36:39 '$4,000', 36:44 '$22,000'; V10 10:04 'eliminate her for money?', 23:23 '$10,000', 23:27 'do another'.

Law 3, Law 4, Law 5, Law 7, Law 9, Law 14 hold at the stated strength. Law 3's '7 of 10 before 1:40' is correct by the list (V1 and V5 later, V9 none). Law 5's mean gaps compute (V1 5.0 min, V3 7.0 min). Law 7's percentages compute (V1 90%, V2 99%, V3 84%). Law 14 is honestly scoped as V1-only with 'Speculation' on generalization.

Hook density is roughly in range once the targets are corrected. Counting the outline's hook: ~13 transitions in 0-12 s (mostly sub-0.3 punch-ins/wipes, matching V1's Phase A which has only 1 true hard cut), 3 in the silent hold, ~10 in 17-30 s, ~4 in 30-45 s = ~18-20 hard cuts + 2 flash-hidden + punch-ins, against a measured 23 at th 0.3 (+3 hidden) in 45 s. It is slightly under-dense in Phase C (10 vs 13) but not structurally off; the dialogue milestones (premise 0:01, prize ≈0:11, wound 0:19, click 0:26/0:29, rule 0:31-0:36, send-off 0:39) map 1:1.

The stage-gate structure itself is sound and consistent with the repo rules: subject lock before spend, seed lock with SHA, hook prototype before any act, hero shots second, act-by-act contact-sheet review, watcher before 1080p, unlisted upload first. Gate 2's 'report actual yield' is the right instrument — it just needs a correct baseline.

No metered-API use is proposed. Grok (subscription), ElevenLabs credits, ChatGPT/Grok image, MMAudio, whisper, FFmpeg and verify_render.py are all subscription or local per feedback_subscriptions_only_no_api_spend.md. The optional real-money viewer giveaway is correctly gated as an owner decision outside the outline. (The Heavy-tier and Remotion items are flagged above as the only leaks.)

Foley approach is correct: MMAudio per shot window, library placement banned, matches feedback_foley_must_be_generated_not_placed and the Grok 'native audio near-silent' finding in reference_seedance_dreamina_2026-09.md.

Fur-covered mouth on GRUFF and a mouthless ORB are genuinely the cheapest lip-sync-proof designs available given feedback_i2v_talking_creature_qa.md (Grok animates creature jaws to dialogue prompts); that part of the cast mitigation is sound even though the rule it cites is the wrong one.
